headline: Braga sack their coach, then travel to Nacional as favourites
summary: Braga go to Nacional on Sunday with a new coach, Franclim Carvalho, appointed after Carlos Vicens was sacked following a third straight defeat. Nacional's run is worse: five defeats in a row. Across 10 bookmakers, with the margin removed, Braga are still clear favourites, though their chance of winning has slipped from 63.3% to 60.2%. The gap in goals has narrowed too: Braga are now rated 0.92 goals better than Nacional, down from 1.07. The goal line is 2.5, with a 50.3% chance of more. Last time we called Braga clear favourites, Gil Vicente won 1-2.
read: Braga arrive at Nacional with a new coach, Franclim Carvalho, after sacking Carlos Vicens and losing three games in a row.

facts.fact: Braga sacked head coach Carlos Vicens with immediate effect and appointed Franclim Carvalho in his place.
facts.meaning: Carvalho's first match in charge is this trip to Nacional, so nobody knows yet how Braga will set up or react.

facts.fact: Braga lost 1-2 at home to Gil Vicente on 19 October, their third defeat in a row.
facts.meaning: A side chasing the European places arrives at Nacional on its worst run of the season so far.

facts.fact: Braga are priced as clear away favourites at 60.2% to win, against 16.4% for Nacional and 23.4% for the draw.
facts.meaning: The market sees Braga as more likely than not to take three points despite their run of defeats.

facts.fact: Braga's chance of winning has come down from 63.3% to 60.2% in recent days.
facts.meaning: They are still clear favourites, but with noticeably less conviction than a few days ago.

facts.fact: Nacional have lost all five of their last matches, a run of LLLLL.
facts.meaning: The hosts are in freefall and have not taken a point since early October.

facts.fact: The market's 50/50 handicap line has moved from Nacional +1.07 to +0.92.
Nacional are 16th of 18 with a goal difference of -9 after eight games.
facts.meaning: Only goal difference separates them from the bottom places, and only one side in the league has conceded more heavily.

facts.fact: Braga have scored three goals in their last five matches.
facts.meaning: For a side priced at 60% to win away, the attacking output has been thin — they are not blowing teams away.

sources.fact: SC Braga sacked head coach Carlos Vicens with immediate effect after a disappointing spell in charge.
Franclim Carvalho was officially appointed as SC Braga's new head coach, succeeding Carlos Vicens.
Braga suffered a third consecutive defeat, losing 1-2 at home to Gil Vicente in the Primeira Liga on 19 October.
Braga president António Salvador described the change from Vicens to Carvalho as a cut rather than a transition.
Braga publicly criticised refereeing as a total loss of direction and demanded higher-level intervention, saying they were harmed against Gil Vicente, Moreirense and Sporting.
New Braga coach Franclim Carvalho said he always had the desire to sit in this position.
Braga's António Salvador received a vote of confidence from the SAD amid a period of contestation.
Vicens said in his farewell that it was a privilege to have been part of something so special at Braga.
